closed subscheme of `grPair` through the mathlib ideal-sheaf machinery — `carveIdealSheaf`
is the kernel ideal sheaf of the disjoint family of chart loci (the largest ideal sheaf
vanishing on all of them, `⨅ over the pair atlas`), and `DivScheme` is its subscheme.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdealSheaf`: the ideal sheaf `I_♦` on `grPair`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme`, `carveSchemeι`, `carveSchemeOver`: the generic glued
  locus, its closed immersion (mathlib's `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` instance), and its
  `Over (Spec k)` form.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker` and
  `carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors`: the factoring criterion at chart tests — a test
  map through a pair chart killing the chart carve ideal factors (uniquely, by `Mono`)
  through `carveSchemeι`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_hom_ext` (`divScheme_hom_ext`, DDR-7's tail): morphisms
  into the locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion.
* **Campaign spellings**: `DivScheme`, `divSchemeι`, `divSchemeOver` at the DAT-D
  windows.

`KeyChart` of the DD-R roadmap) rests on the landed gluing compatibility
(`carveIdeal_le_ker_of_specMap_pairChartMap_eq`); its remaining half is the app-level
localization bookkeeping and is left to the successor lane (see the inbox memory).

10	# A connected divisor can be certified only inside a single pinned chart
11	
12	The two preceding files bracket the certificate assembler's per-piece no-leak clause:
13	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows it forces the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to
14	be closed, and `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` shows the "swallow or miss" shape produces it.
15	This file closes the bracket, and thereby decides the lane's satisfiability question.
16	
17	The observation is that leak-freeness *plus connectedness of the divisor* already implies
18	swallow-or-miss.  For each piece the trace `supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support
19	(the piece is open) and closed in it (that is leak-freeness), so a connected support leaves
20	only the two degenerate values: the trace is empty, or it is everything.  Feeding this into
21	the chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` and `relCover_sup` gives
22	
23	> **a nonempty connected divisor whose adaptation is leak-free at every piece lies inside
24	> `V₀` or inside `V₁`.**
25	
26	That is the satisfiability verdict the lane never obtained.  It is not a statement about
27	pieces, adaptations, tubes or fibres: it says the certificate interface can only ever be
28	satisfied by divisors confined to one pinned chart of `pi` — a **chart-design** condition.
29	
30	Nor can a shrink of the base repair it, because base localization does not disconnect the
31	divisor: `Spec (R[x]/(x² − t))` over `R = k[t]` is connected over every basic open of
32	`Spec R`, so no Zariski neighbourhood of `t = 0` splits the divisor into clopen packets.
33	Hence the "clopen packet extraction" programme (memory I-0209) is available exactly when the
34	divisor is already chart-confined, and the honest obligation of the lane is to make the
35	DD-R atlas produce chart-confined divisors.
36

39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak` —
40	  leak-freeness at a piece plus a connected support forces swallow-or-miss at that piece.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected` — the
42	  same for every piece at once, i.e. leak-free + connected ⟹ swallow-or-miss.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` — **the
44	  satisfiability verdict**: a nonempty connected support with a leak-free adaptation lies
45	  inside one of the two pinned charts.

74	/-- **A connected support leaves a leak-free piece no middle ground.** The trace

77

80	itself and the complement of the — closed — trace. -/
81	theorem subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak (j : A.index)
82	    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
83	    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
84	    d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
85	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
86	  classical
87	  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :=
88	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak
89	  -- the two separating opens: the piece, and the complement of the (closed) trace
90	  by_cases hdisj : Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
91	  · exact Or.inr hdisj
92	  refine Or.inl ?_
93	  by_contra hnsub
94	  -- both halves are nonempty, so preconnectedness produces a point in their intersection
95	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := Set.not_disjoint_iff.mp hdisj
96	  obtain ⟨y, hyS, hyU⟩ := Set.not_subset.mp hnsub
97	  obtain ⟨z, hzS, hzu, hzv⟩ :=
98	    hconn (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
99	      (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))ᶜ
100	      (A.pieces j).isOpen hclosed.isOpen_compl
101	      (fun w hw => by
102	        by_cases hwU : w ∈ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
103	        · exact Or.inl hwU
104	        · exact Or.inr fun hc => hwU hc.2)
105	      ⟨x, hx.1, hx.2⟩ ⟨y, hyS, fun hc => hyU hc.2⟩
106	  exact hzv ⟨hzS, hzu⟩
107

109	hypothesis of `forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` is not an extra assumption for a
110	connected divisor: it is what leak-freeness already says. -/
111	theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected
112	    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
113	    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
114	    ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
115	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := fun j =>
116	  A.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak j hconn (hleak j)
117

119	
120	/-- **A nonempty connected divisor with a leak-free adaptation lies inside one pinned
121	chart.** The verdict the certificate lane needed: since `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` (`relCover_sup`), the
122	two chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` cannot both land on their `Disjoint`
123	branch for a nonempty support.
124	
125	Consequently the certificate interface `IsCertified` — whose per-piece clause (c1) forces
126	leak-freeness — is satisfiable for a connected divisor **only** if that divisor avoids
127	`pi⁻¹(∞)` (so it sits in `V₀`) or avoids `pi⁻¹(0)` (so it sits in `V₁`).  This is a
128	condition on the divisor and the chosen `pi`; the adaptation, the support tube, the packet
129	idempotents and the base shrink are all irrelevant to it. -/
130	theorem supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected
131	    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hne : d.supportLocus.Nonempty)
132	    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
133	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
134	      ∨ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
135	  have hswallow := A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected hconn hleak
136	  rcases A.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀ hswallow with h₀ | h₀
137	  · exact Or.inl h₀
138	  -- the support misses `V₀`, so `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` puts all of it in `V₁`
139	  refine Or.inr fun x hx => ?_
140	  have hmem : x ∈ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
141	      ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) := by
142	    rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
143	  rcases (Opens.mem_sup ..).mp hmem with h | h

155	    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hne : d.supportLocus.Nonempty)

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivCarveLocus
7	
8	/-!
9	# DDR-3 anchor — the universal carve pair over the `Z(♦)`-chart rings
10	
11	The input side of the relative local-generator construction
12	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3; I-0193 "notes for DDR-3"): each chart of `DivScheme g`
13	is `Spec` of the **carve chart ring** `R_Z = R_{I,J} ⧸ I_♦`, and the tautological pair
14	pushes to a universal Grassmannian pair over it which satisfies the carve after *every*
15	base change — in particular in every residue-field fibre, which is exactly where P-fib
16	(`RiemannRoch/PFib.lean`) takes over.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivCarveChartRing` — the `Z(♦)`-chart ring, with its Noetherian
19	  instance (`isNoetherianRing_pairChartRing` + quotient), the DDR-3 licence;
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divCarveChartMk` — the quotient presentation, as a `k`-algebra map;
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divUniversalFst/Snd` — **the universal pair**: the tautological
22	  pair pushed to the chart ring along `divCarveChartMk` (`Module.Grassmannian.map`);
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` — the kill law: any algebra over the
24	  chart ring kills `I_♦`;
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divUniversal_carve` — **the universal carve law**: over any algebra
26	  `S` of the chart ring, the pulled-back tautological pair satisfies `(♦)` (through the
27	  DDR-1 keystone `carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map`); stated over instance arguments
28	  `[Algebra R_{I,J} S] [IsScalarTower …]` per the recorded `Grassmannian.map` seam
29	  discipline (I-0193 hazard 6) — consumers instantiate with `w.toAlgebra`;
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divUniversal_carve_residueField` — **the fibrewise carve** at every
31	  prime of the chart ring: the pair `(K_M ⊗ κ(p), K' ⊗ κ(p))` satisfies the carve over
32	  `κ(p)` — the hypothesis package P-fib's `existsUnique_effective_divisor_of_carve`
33	  consumes fibrewise (with the window/corank data supplied by the DD-4 transport seam).
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open TensorProduct CategoryTheory
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	open Grassmannian Scheme
45	
46	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
47	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
48	variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
49	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
50	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
51	
52	/-- **The `Z(♦)`-chart ring** `R_Z = R_{I,J} ⧸ I_♦`: the coordinate ring of the
53	chart-wise carve locus `divCarveLocus` (`Spec` of this ring is `carveLocus` at the
54	campaign multipliers). -/
55	abbrev DivCarveChartRing (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) : Type u :=
56	  PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j ⧸ divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
57	
58	/-- **The DDR-3 Noetherian licence**: the `Z(♦)`-chart rings are Noetherian (finite type
59	over `k`: quotient of the Noetherian pair chart ring). -/
60	instance isNoetherianRing_divCarveChartRing
61	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
62	    IsNoetherianRing (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) :=
63	  inferInstance
64	
65	/-- The quotient presentation of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring, as a `k`-algebra map. -/
66	noncomputable def divCarveChartMk (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
67	    PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →ₐ[k] DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j :=
68	  Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ k (divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j)
69	
70	/-- **The universal first window** `K_M^{univ}` over a `Z(♦)`-chart ring: the
71	tautological chart-`I` window pushed to the quotient. -/
72	noncomputable def divUniversalFst (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
73	    grFunctorAff k (Fin r₁ → k) g (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) :=
74	  Module.Grassmannian.map (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j)
75	    (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j)
76	
77	/-- **The universal second window** `K'^{univ}` over a `Z(♦)`-chart ring: the
78	tautological chart-`J` window pushed to the quotient. -/
79	noncomputable def divUniversalSnd (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
80	    grFunctorAff k (Fin r₂ → k) g (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) :=
81	  Module.Grassmannian.map (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j)
82	    (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j)
83	
84	/-- **The kill law**: every algebra of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring kills the carve ideal (the
85	algebra map factors through the quotient by the scalar tower). -/
86	theorem divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower
87	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) (S : Type u) [CommRing S]
88	    [Algebra (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S]
89	    [Algebra (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) S]
90	    [IsScalarTower (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j)
91	      (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) S] :
92	    divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
93	      ≤ RingHom.ker (algebraMap (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S) := by
94	  intro x hx
95	  rw [RingHom.mem_ker, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j)
96	    (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) S, Ideal.Quotient.algebraMap_eq,
97	    Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hx, map_zero]
98	
99	/-- **The universal carve law** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3, the input): over any
100	algebra `S` of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring, the pulled-back tautological pair satisfies the
101	carve `(♦)` — for every multiplier section `s ∈ H⁰(𝒪(A))` the carve-pair arrow of the
102	base-changed pair vanishes.  This is the DDR-1 keystone
103	`carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map` fed by the kill law; the instance-argument spelling is
104	the recorded `Grassmannian.map` seam discipline (consumers instantiate `[Algebra R_{I,J}
105	S]` with `w.toAlgebra` and the tower with `IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'`). -/
106	theorem divUniversal_carve
107	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) (S : Type u) [CommRing S]
108	    [Algebra k S] [Algebra (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S]
109	    [IsScalarTower k (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j) S]
110	    [Algebra (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) S]
111	    [IsScalarTower (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j)
112	      (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j) S]
113	    (s : ↥(divisorSections k A ⊤)) :
114	    carvePairArrow (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ s)
115	      (LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ S
116	        (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule))
117	      (LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ S
118	        (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule)) = 0 :=
119	  (carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j S).mp
120	    (divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j S) s
121	
122	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
123	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8 in
124	-- the canonical residue-field tower `k → R_{I,J} → κ(q)` (localization + quotient
125	-- composites over the `MvPolynomial` tensor chart ring) exceeds the default search
126	-- budget and the project-default pending depth (the recorded in-file escape hatch)
127	/-- **The fibrewise carve** (the P-fib input, `informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 3): at
128	every point of the chart-wise carve locus — a prime `q` of the pair chart ring
129	containing `I_♦` — the tautological pair pulled back to the residue field `κ(q)`
130	satisfies the carve.  (Points of the `Z(♦)`-chart correspond to such primes; this
131	spelling stays on the pair chart ring, where all `κ(q)`-instances are the cheap
132	canonical ones.)  This is the hypothesis package P-fib's
133	`existsUnique_effective_divisor_of_carve` consumes fibrewise, with the window/corank
134	data supplied by the DD-4 transport seam. -/
135	theorem divUniversal_carve_residueField
136	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
137	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j))
138	    (hq : divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≤ q.asIdeal)
139	    (s : ↥(divisorSections k A ⊤)) :
140	    carvePairArrow (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ s)
141	      (LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ q.asIdeal.ResidueField
142	        (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule))
143	      (LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ q.asIdeal.ResidueField
144	        (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j).toSubmodule)) = 0 :=
145	  (carveIdeal_le_ker_iff_carve_map k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j
146	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField).mp
147	    (hq.trans (Ideal.ker_algebraMap_residueField (I := q.asIdeal)).symm.le) s
148	
149	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# From pointwise away-certificates to a span-`⊤` family

`DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` reduced the DD-R certificate gate to *away-local* certificates
over a span-`⊤` family.  The geometry that produces such certificates, however, is
pointwise on the base: the support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
isolates the pieces over a Zariski neighbourhood **of one base point at a time**, and the
fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.

This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.

The result is that the certificate gate for the DD-R endgame is now genuinely *pointwise*:
one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate
  for a bare local-equation system.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified`
  — the seed form.
-/

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`
holds at some element outside each prime, then finitely many elements satisfying `P` span
`⊤`.  This is quasi-compactness of `Spec R` in the elementary form the certificate gate
needs: the basic opens of the good elements cover the spectrum, hence the good set spans
the unit ideal, hence `1` is a finite combination of good elements. -/
theorem exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime (P : R → Prop)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ P r) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, P (g i) := by
  classical
  -- the good elements span the unit ideal, because their basic opens cover `Spec R`
  have hspan : Ideal.span {r : R | P r} = ⊤ := by
    rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff']
    refine top_le_iff.mp fun p _ => ?_
    obtain ⟨r, hrp, hrP⟩ := h p
    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨r, by
      simpa only [Opens.mem_iSup, PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen] using ⟨hrP, hrp⟩⟩
  -- `1` is then a finite combination of good elements
  have hone : (1 : R) ∈ Submodule.span R {r : R | P r} := by
    show (1 : R) ∈ Ideal.span {r : R | P r}
    rw [hspan]; exact Submodule.mem_top
  obtain ⟨T, hTsub, hT⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_finite_of_mem_span hone
  refine ⟨T.card, fun i => (T.equivFin.symm i : R), ?_, fun i => hTsub (T.equivFin.symm i).2⟩
  have hrange : Set.range (fun i : Fin T.card => ((T.equivFin.symm i : R))) = (T : Set R) := by
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
      exact (T.equivFin.symm i).2
    · intro hx
      exact ⟨T.equivFin ⟨x, hx⟩, by simp⟩

hypothesis of `seedUniv'` / `isGenerator_seedUniv'`: at every point `z`, the seed colength

`SeedUnivRDN` follows from the **single honest input** — seed-level germ divisibility

  `∀ z, ∀ ψ ∈ K_univ, germ_z (read ψ) ∈ ⟨germ_z (read (sec z))⟩`   (in the stalk `𝒪_z`),

i.e. the achiever's `read sec z` (which attains the base multiplicity at `z`, I-0291, hence has

per-point germ reduction `notMem_support_chartColengthModule_of_forall_germ_mem_span` and the
window finiteness `finite_divUniversalSeedK`.  Single-point throughout — the degree obstruction

(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f), the DD-1c inverse-law adjudication)

The forward map `divFamDivisor` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField`) sends a
certified divisor family over the field `K` to its Weil divisor, and is `DivEq`-invariant
(`Scheme.presentationDivisor_eq_of_divEq`). This file lands the **converse** and the
**injectivity** it powers, and packages the **equiv reduction** — the exact assembly of the
frozen `divFamFieldEquiv` from the two remaining, precisely-named gaps.

* `Scheme.divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq` — the **converse of DivEq-invariance**: two
  local-equation systems on the curve with the *same* Weil divisor are divisor-equal. On the
  common refinement of the two covers the ratio of the anchor equations is a unit at every
  closed point (equal orders read the equal divisor coefficient off any piece,
  `MeromorphicPresentation.ordZ_elem_eq` + `coeffAt_presentationDivisor`), hence — being an
  `𝒪(0)`-section together with its inverse (`exists_section_germ_eq`) — a genuine unit
  section that rescales one system to the other. Together with the landed
  `presentationDivisor_eq_of_divEq` this is the characterization
  `DivEq d₁ d₂ ↔ presentationDivisor d₁ = presentationDivisor d₂`.

* `divFamDivisor_injective` — the **forward map is injective**: two families with equal
  divisor are `DivEq`, hence equal in the setoid `DivFam`. This is *unconditional* (no
  Mayer–Vietoris, no backward construction); it is the injective half of `divFamFieldEquiv`,
  and it *is* the second inverse law `divFamOfDivisor (divFamDivisor F) = F` once the
  backward map exists (both sides then present the same divisor).

* `divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj` — the **equiv reduction**: given the two remaining gaps —
  `hdeg` (the general colength↔degree identity `deg (divFamDivisor F) = n` for an *arbitrary*
  certified family, the honest Mayer–Vietoris wall) and `hsurj` (backward realization: every
  effective degree-`n` divisor is the divisor of some certified family, discharged over `K`
  by the support-separated construction whose certificate rank is `deg = n` *for free* via
  `deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated`, no general MV) — the equiv

inverse law (that is landed here as `divFamDivisor_injective`):

The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),
whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`
carries certified families over the localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` which are
divisor-equal to the pulled system.  **Nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a
certificate over `R` itself.**

`(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` over the chart ring `R_Z`, whose no-leak input
is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
its consumer needs.

This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`
specializes it to a seed: if the seed's adaptation acquires a certificate **after
localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support
tube produces (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`: piece isolation is available
Zariski-locally on the base, never globally) — then the seed's own system is locally
certified, and hence has a `DivFamZar` class.

The mathematical content is the observation that `IsLocallyCertified` is designed to be
produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is
`DivEq` to the pulled adaptation's system on the nose; the localization step that makes
no-leak true is licensed here rather than being an unrecoverable obstruction.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — the span-`⊤` production

genuine weakening of the old gate rather than a parallel track. -/

    (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified n) :
